newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish debt/currency market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Swedish debt/currency market closing report.

text.p: Swedish debt yields made a firm start on Wednesday following gains in U.S. Treasuries.
The 10-year bond yield fell nearly ten basis point when the market opened. But after an initial rush, buying faded out as dealers looked for further guidance from New York.

"Buyers jumped in quickly to catch up with the U.S. move on Tuesday. Although the market still has a firm undertone, I think we need more foreign support to take yields down from these levels," one dealer said.
Ten-year bond yields ended nine basis points lower at 6.41 percent. Six-month T-bill rates closed flat at 4.25 percent.
T-bills were hit by poor demand in a ten billion crown T-bill auction. The National Debt Office cut the six-month issue from the planned five billion crowns to 1.9 billion crowns.
The crown benefitted from the stronger dollar. The mark eased against the crown to 4.2815 from 4.3030 late Tuesday.

"We saw more buying from New York dealers this afternoon and I think the crown can gain further. But it's hard to predict a level, since we passed the last support at 4.29 crowns versus the mark and now are in uncharted territory," said one dealer.
